newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent slightly higher, profit taking seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent slightly higher, profit taking seen.

text.p: June Brent crude futures in Asia were untraded in late trading on Tuesday but were quoted steady in generally cautious talk ahead of London.
June Brent on SIMEX was quoted at $19.65/$19.80 per barrel, after London gained 79 cents to settle at $19.72. July traded at $19.52, up five cents.

Brokers said an overnight rise was backed by strong breaking news, including earthquakes in Iran, Iran war games in the Gulf, OPEC ministers saying they wanted to bolster prices and worries about disruption to North Sea Brent loadings at Sullom Voe.
Brokers said the rise overnight could tempt some quick profit taking, although technical charts were supporting the market.
"There could be a small dip down but I think any dip will be seen as an area of purchase," one broker said.
In addition, news that once again Shell has shut flow stations in Nigeria owing to a tribal fued was likely to support the market, especially amid a tightening Atlantic Basin market.
